Use case: stylized-concept. One exquisitely crafted collectible illustration for NOSFY, portrait 2:3 full art, ideally 1024x1536, no frame or text. Third predefined family: LES BOIS SANS LUNE / THE MOONLESS WOODS.
Signature: an almost impossibly dense ANCIENT BLACK PINE FOREST, tangled roots, bark, needles, dead leaves and tiny claustrophobic clearings. The forest canopy encloses the world. Camera always beneath trees, no vast panorama, no mountains, no visible moon or sky. Deep dark organic forest shapes fill the image edge to edge. Cold true monochrome: velvet BLACK, coal gray, charcoal, VERY SPARSE muted WHITE NACRE. No orange, no embers, no fire, no blue, no green, no purple, no multicolored holographic shine, no silver snowfall. This must be instantly different from a black-orange volcanic family and from an open misty moonlit forest valley.
Mood and medium: haunting, poetic, intimate dark fine-art fantasy illustration, exquisite tactile materials and expressive living creatures, slight stylization, no generic wildlife photograph. Black masses separated by subtle grayscale midtones, selected tiny grazing highlights reveal rich detail and readable face/silhouette at small card size. At least three quarters of picture profoundly dark, no white fog wall or bright sky. Beauty discovered inside darkness. Do not make everything equally glossy: matte blacks provide the setting for tiny precious nacre reflections.
Landscape and scene are unified by roots, bark and needles. No constructed objects, equipment, jewelry, armor, runes, logo, text, watermark, UI, border or rarity symbols. No gore, skulls or grotesque horror. Full subject with important parts safely within central 80 percent width and height; generous dark breathing space around extremities. No creature parts clipped. Each rarity retains outstanding craftsmanship but spectacle and material richness rise clearly from common to legendary.
COMMON LANDSCAPE — a very beautiful, understated collectible place, not an animal card. No creature, people or face hidden in the trees.
A very small circular clearing buried in an overwhelmingly dense forest of ancient black pines. Foreground immense gnarled roots curl over a bed of matte dark needles and fallen leaves, forming a delicate natural threshold. In the midground a broad old pine has a split trunk with a narrow dark opening at its base, and a thin still mirror-black pool gathers among its roots. Just three or four pale fallen leaves rest at the pool edge, minute dew beads on their finely veined surfaces catch a faint soft gray-white reflection from a hidden slit high in the canopy. Nothing glows by magic. Behind: layer upon layer of tall charcoal trunks almost swallow the clearing, overlapping branches interlace until the sky is completely concealed. A single faint low wisp of DARK gray ground mist separates the back trees, never milky white.
Very thoughtful composition, large quiet black areas and a modest path of reflected light leading into the clearing. Uneven bark striations, delicate dead-leaf veins, tangled root surfaces, pine needles and water reflections extremely carefully painted where light reaches them. Soft haunting stillness, damp organic texture, black depth. Restrained matte finish with tiny nacre-like dewdrops only, no shiny crystals, no excessive sparkles. The beauty of a COMMON comes from composition, place and delicate craft. This is not a nighttime photograph with daylight exposure, not snowy woodland, not a lunar valley landscape.

RARE CREATURE — one exquisite black bat slowly glides between close ancient pine trunks, wings lifted into a delicate vertical arc and whole animal entirely inside the frame. Wings span only 72 percent of image width, both complete tips visible with comfortable margin. Fine dark furry face, tall tapering ears, soft alert eyes with tiny smoky-white reflections, two natural hind feet. Beautifully uncanny and endearing, not fangs and snarling.
Precious understated SHINY treatment: membranes of translucent SMOKED BLACK PEARL, intricate charcoal veins, microscopic soft ivory nacre inclusions buried inside glass-dark tissue. Only a few thin wing veins and small material facets catch DISCREET off-white opalescent light, never entire white wings, never rainbow. A singular crescent-shaped pattern of very fine pale pinpricks runs near the inside edge of each wing, like dew in spider silk; the pattern remains sparse and organic, no symbols. Matte-black fur contrasts with softly reflective wing membranes. Every finger joint and membrane fold anatomically coherent and lavishly detailed, whiskers fine and face expressive.
Creature emerges from the narrow gap between intertwined roots and a hollow pine trunk, with close rough dark bark behind and fine suspended charcoal mist below. Tiny highlights connect bat wing material to damp bark and leaves; the world stays almost entirely black. Mood of a secret nocturnal encounter, exquisitely controlled low light, high quality fine-art painting, not a flash-lit bat photo. Distinctly more precious than common landscape, no colossal wings or explosive magical energy.

EPIC CREATURE — one tall powerful ancient black wolf emerges slowly from between densely entwined roots of colossal pine trees. Full coherent four-legged body and one tail visible, three-quarter forward stride, face turned slightly toward viewer. Very dark forest presses tightly around the creature, no opening onto a landscape. Low elegant viewpoint and enormous nearby trunks provide dramatic scale. Keep ears, paws and tail within frame with generous margins.
Memorable identity: a long windless mane of velvet black strands whose tips curl subtly into rootlike tendrils; organic ridged dark bark pattern in the coarse fur along its shoulders, continuous with living skin, not wooden armor and not a tree growing from its back. White-gray eyes with restrained light, an expressive solemn animal face, exquisite nostril/whisker detail. Only the crown of its mane and a thin line at the cheek carry soft cold nacre fibers; its back reveals narrow shimmering mother-of-pearl streaks as faint reflected light grazes it. The SHINY effect is beautiful BLACK PEARL with DISCREET WHITE, not a white wolf, not silver armor, no electric glowing streaks. Almost all its body stays rich matte or satin charcoal.
Under its paws, layered dark leaves, needles, twisting roots and small wet black stones; an extremely thin vein of reflected white light threads between roots, reflected water not magic. The nearest trees loom like shadow columns, roots echo the wolf silhouette. Fine-art painterly chiaroscuro, tactile microdetail in selected lit surfaces, mysterious depth and beautiful presence. More epic in scale and singularity than the bat, still less monumental than the legendary raven. No snow, sparks, fire or orange eyes.

LEGENDARY CREATURE — an utterly breathtaking immense BLACK RAVEN, ancient sovereign spirit of a dense lightless pine forest. Make a legendary raven, not an ordinary bird, not an eagle and not a dragon. Exquisite narrow slightly curved raven beak, intelligent expressive dark face, calm intense pale-smoke eyes with tiny soft white catchlights. It sits on a great arch of intertwined living roots among towering black pines, wings raised in a grand tall arch as if the entire forest has quietly awakened. Body, two coherent claws, LONG elegant tail and BOTH ENTIRE WINGTIPS visible with generous dark margin: the complete spread spans at most 78 percent of canvas width and 75 percent of height. No wings cut by any edge.
The creature's extraordinary silhouette: elongated flight feathers fan into intricately layered black plumes, each feather branches only in its fine barbs, their contours subtly echoing pine needles and dark boughs; no literal tree branches glued onto wings. Feathers range from deep velvet matte to the most luxurious polished jet and BLACK MOTHER-OF-PEARL. Legendary SHINY detail: very fine soft WHITE NACRE filaments live inside selected feather surfaces; tiny broken ivory reflections trace a few arcs of the wings and the eye feathers, like a black pearl momentarily turned into dim light. Extremely sophisticated micro-optics: dark pearlescent depth, mirror-black planes, faint milky reflections almost lost in the black. NOT a white raven, NOT silver wings, NO bright halo and NO starburst glitter. Around 90 percent of plumage remains black. Lavish detail in individually overlapping flight feathers, age-worn beak, silky fine face featherlets and subtly opalescent feather shafts. This is the most precious material in the family but the most controlled light.
The full forest surrounds it: colossal pine bark columns, nearly invisible black needles overhead, tangled roots across lower foreground, layers of trunks receding into charcoal shadow. A few small pale fallen leaves near the claws emphasize scale, sparse fine mist remains dark. Majestic vertical fine-art composition, intense yet tender ancient living gaze, enormous quiet presence, an unforgettable creature one would feel attached to. Visually extraordinary and profoundly dark, no light sky, no moon, mountains, jewelry, tiara, magical symbols or flashy effects.
